pr_body:
Closes #66656.

Current, `Docker#verifyOssInstallation(...)` checks the permissions of
`elasticsearch.keystore`, however this often causes problems when a test
forgets to wait for ES and the keystore doesn't exist yet.

Instead, add a test specifically to check `elasticsearch.keystore` and
remove the check from `verifyOssInstallation()`.

comments:
Another one, but on ubuntu-18.04: https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/jkuoddwnkjkzs

This test [fails](https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/scans/tests?search.relativeStartTime=P7D&search.timeZoneId=Australia/Melbourne&tests.container=org.elasticsearch.packaging.test.DockerTests&tests.sortField=FAILED&tests.test=test085EnvironmentVariablesAreRespectedUnderDockerExec&tests.unstableOnly=true) almost everyday since 2020-12-30 and the OS are fedora 32, debian 9 and ubuntu 18.04.

@pugnascotia is this at all similar to these failures?

https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/scans/tests?search.relativeStartTime=P28D&search.tags=not:pull-request&search.timeZoneId=America/Los_Angeles&tests.container=org.elasticsearch.packaging.test.DockerTests&tests.disabledDistributions=WyJvdXRjb21lOnNraXBwZWQiLCJvdXRjb21lOnBhc3NlZCJd&tests.sortField=FAILED&tests.test=test010Install&tests.unstableOnly=true

@mark-vieira Yes, though I'm a little dismayed to see another failure.

I think we (or rather, I) need to change this so that the keystore permissions are explicitly checked in a dedicated test, and remove the check from `verifyOssInstallation()` because it's too easy to cause problems.

There was a number of failures on `DockerTests test010Install` over the weekend with the same missing file exception:

`stat: cannot stat '/usr/share/elasticsearch/config/elasticsearch.keystore': No such file or directory`

https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/wpnezgpi6h5fu
https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/c3ah7462xlnz6

These were all on 7.x using the successful commit 27744169228f43592f94cd313606fa9718760362 which contains the backport of the fix in abc645424bbb36273108474d04b219469f44f30d
Both those build scans indicate `7.11`, not `7.x`. I'll backport the fix to `7.11` as well, which I should have done in the first place TBH.

review_comments: I think "compatibile" is the right word when describing Docker.
Are there no other files that get laid down on startup? It's just the keystore?
Besides log files, it's just the keystore AFAIK.

The failures seem to indicate that `waitForElasticseach()` doesn't seem to be robust enough. Do we have theories on why that method would return, but the keystore file would _not_ be there? Wouldn't we expect this test to occasionally fail still?

I'm not sure that `waitForElasticseach()` is the problem. The original problem in #66656 was due to to the test running a CLI tool without waiting for ES to start up and create the keystore, which in this case the tool needed.

I removed the keystore from the `verifyOssInstallation()` because most tests don't care about it, and have a test fail because it didn't wait for a file to be created that the test doesn't care about is just...silly.

Sure, I guess my point being that the new test you added is still susceptible to the same underlying cause of those other failures, unless I'm missing something. Indeed I agree we don't need superfluous assertions in those other tests, so if nothing else this should fail _less_ often. We'll keep an eye on it.
Basically this - if the new test is failing often, at least I have somewhere more specific to start investigating.
